method: Coordinated Terra subagents with primary-agent raw-event, pointer-arithmetic, and cross-stream review. Passive supported front-door observation only.

safety.elevation: Owner-authorized hidden elevated PowerShell ran only python tools/f1c_mod.py read-only observers.

pit_route.conclusion: Every raw selector-entry pointer was record-base aligned. Neither record 983 nor 984 was sampled; their (1,18) effect remains unproven.

normal_sampled_sequence: fuel rises to PitTargetFuel during status 3

combined_two_hz.job_field_observations: PitRefuelFlag and PitTyreChangeFlag were 1 and PitWingChangeFlag was 0 at captured transitions. PitRepairFlag changed 1->0 twice during sampled status 3; labels are not promoted beyond correlation.

pit_service.unclassified_event: One 5 Hz slot-5 trace sampled status 2->0 after 7.032 seconds, with fuel rise and CallToBox clear but no sampled status 3. No completion/cancellation/retirement meaning is assigned.
pit_service.late_cluster_limit: Late 2 Hz status 2->4 samples followed the last lap increment and may omit an intermediate state or reflect accelerated post-running completion. They do not prove a new direct state-machine edge.

lifecycle_control.conclusion: The late return-to-pits cluster followed the last lap increment but produced no AIW rebuild, allocation relocation, reparse, or proven session boundary.

event_node_capture.conclusion: Natural passage through both static (1,18) event records is directly observed with PathSelector=1 and CallToBox=1. The downstream consumer effect remains unisolated.

physical_service.conclusion: Physical tread refresh and front-wing restoration outcomes are observed at the service boundary. Exact internal job ordering and next-compound semantics remain open.

post_restart_aiw.conclusion: The same AIW addresses were observed after restart; no-reparse cannot be distinguished from same-address allocator reuse because the boundary was not continuously captured.
